summary: Camp lookout from 1932, CCC-built wooden tower in 1935, present 67-ft steel live-in tower from 1964; on tribal land, permit needed.

access.note: On Colville Indian Reservation land. Non-tribal visitors need a Colville recreation permit (trail guide: $80 a year). The 2021 fire burned Keller Butte Road north of the lookout and may affect access from that side.

visit.trail_note: Easiest route is from the south shore of Buffalo Lake along BIA 21, then over to Keller Butte Road. Clay roads turn slick and impassable when wet.

events.note: Camp lookout established at Keller Butte; a July 1932 newspaper item reported a man to be sent to the new station
First CCC camp for the district opened with 75 men; one crew was to build a road from the summit to the new lookout tower
CCC built an 80-foot three-legged wooden tower with a 7x7 cab and an L-4 ground cabin for living quarters. An August 1935 newspaper said 90 feet.
Teachers worked as summer fire lookouts; Miss Josephine Volger stationed on Keller Butte
Inspection found the 1935 tower and shelter unsound and unsafe; proposed a 65-foot steel tower with quarters on top
Present 67-foot steel live-in tower built; staffed every summer
Chuweah Creek fire, started by lightning July 12, 2021; burned across Keller Butte Road north of the lookout; contained at more than 36,000 acres; lookout survived unharmed

corrections.why: L-4 names the ground cabin built with the 1935 wooden tower. The register, trail guide and fire lookout page describe the current structure as a 67-foot steel live-in tower built in 1964.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An August 1935 newspaper called the new tower 90 feet; the register and the 1960 inspection both give 80 feet for the wooden tower built that year.

notes_for_editor: Elevation differs across sources: 4,800 ft (register; record's 1,463 m matches), 4,811 ft (trail guide summit) and 4,831 ft (fire lookout page and 1960 inspection, which refers to the old tower). Height: the 1935 tower is 80 ft in the register, trail guide and 1960 inspection, but an August 1935 newspaper said 90 ft. The 1960 proposal was a 65-ft steel tower; the present tower is 67 ft. Permit fee comes from a guide last updated March 2024; confirm with the Colville Confederated Tribes. The register page carries 1960 photos (three-leg tower and L-4 cabin, courtesy of the National Archive) with no image URLs in the cache, so none added; check NARA licensing if wanted. The weebly and firelookout URLs returned the same content pattern as Johnny George; confirm URL-to-title pairs before publishing. The record's design correction is proposed, not applied. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the 2021 ignition sentence no longer cites the trail guide, which supports only the fire's effect on access and the lookout's survival; evidence added for the 1932, 1933, 1935 and 1943 items.
